targets.text: the Thor cortex gets speculative decoding back — DSpark or MTP, behind the Triton GDN decode path

VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=triton actually prevents the fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp launch on sm_110 under a real speculative batch. Verified by BOOTING the Thor cortex with triton set plus any --speculative-config and completing a multi-token decode — the d1 failure surfaced on the FIRST decode, so a healthy /health is not evidence. Falsified if the same 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device' RuntimeError appears, in which case the whole frame collapses to a negative result and is reported as one

VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=triton is the unlock, and it is a first-class vLLM env var (envs.py:131 and :1211, Literal['cuda','triton'], default 'cuda'). qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:491-505 reads it, and :1807 makes 'gdn_decode_kernel == cuda' a REQUIRED conjunct of the fused-MTP gate — so setting triton routes the target's GDN layers down _forward_core (the Triton spec path) and the missing-image kernel is never launched. This turns the d1 'MTP MUST BE OFF on sm_110' blocker from a hard wall into a config knob, and it applies to MTP-n2 and DSpark alike

setting VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=triton is sufficient on its own — no source patch, no image change. Verified by the arm-B boot completing a multi-token decode with --speculative-config present. Falsified if the boot still crashes, or if vLLM raises 'VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=cuda is not supported' style config errors that reveal a second required knob

the vLLM build already on the Thor declares the method: probing vllm.config.speculative.SpeculativeMethod inside the running model-gear-vllm-primary lists 'dspark' (and 'dflash'), on the identical build string (0.26.1rc1.dev942+g5a4c8d992) the Spark's 2026-08-24 spike ran. No image change is needed to try this — only argv and one env var

no image bump is needed. Verified by the DSpark arm loading DSparkDraftModel on the Thor's currently pinned digest 8bd082c274fa. Falsified if the drafter fails to resolve, in which case the spike scope grows to an image change and should stop for a decision

the 1M YaRN window and DSpark cannot both survive on the Thor. The Spark refused the DSpark boot at max_model_len=1048576 / util 0.58 ('needs 51.47 GiB KV; available 40.76'), and the Thor is strictly worse per GiB of KV: it runs kv_cache_dtype=auto (the validated #109 divergence) where the Spark runs fp8, and its 1M pool is 1,114,504 tokens vs the Spark's 1,271,476 at the same util. So any Thor speculation arm inherits the same forced trade-down to the checkpoint's native 262144 — a served-contract change visible through lobes capabilities, not a private dial

262144 is genuinely the ceiling for a DSpark arm on this box. Verified by the DSpark arm booting at 262144 and, if headroom looks generous, one probe boot above it to record where vLLM actually refuses. Falsified if DSpark boots comfortably at a larger window, in which case the trade-down was over-conservative and the served contract should be revisited

PR #202 has ALREADY changed what the Thor would render, and nobody measured it on sm_110. The d1 transcript records the Thor deployment as 'lobes init --shape spark-lobe --apply --force on the thor card', so the Thor borrows spark-lobe — the very shape 830bbf3 moved to DSpark @ 262144. A routine re-render on the Thor today would arm DSpark argv on a box where the fused GDN MTP kernel has no image, AND silently drop the served window from 1M to 262144. This is the spark-lobe re-render trap that docs/dspark-speculation.md point 8 closed for the Spark, still open in the opposite direction for the Thor

the Thor really does render spark-lobe. Verified by reading LOBES_SHAPE / the shape provenance in ~/.lobes/.env and by a dry-run 'lobes init --shape spark-lobe --profile thor' diffed against the deployed compose. Falsified if the Thor renders something else, in which case this boundary is withdrawn

the Thor's deployed compose predates the PRIMARY_SPECULATIVE_CONFIG slot: grep of ~/.lobes/docker-compose.yml finds only MULTIMODAL_SPECULATIVE_CONFIG expanded, and the .env carries no PRIMARY_SPECULATIVE_CONFIG line — MTP is off there by a hand-edit that deleted the hardcoded flag, exactly the deployment defect docs/dspark-speculation.md point 7 found on the Spark. So arming any drafter on the Thor requires re-rendering the compose first, which is the same operation that carries the spark-lobe trap above. Sequence them deliberately

the measurement itself is the win, independent of the outcome. Today the Thor's cortex — the fleet's reasoning/deciding/final-authority lobe — runs with NO speculative decoding at all because d1 recorded 'MTP MUST BE OFF on sm_110' as a flat kernel-gap fact. Whether speculation turns out to be worth deploying or not, this run replaces that flat fact with a measured, conditioned answer, and gives the repo its first sm_110 evidence for the Triton GDN decode path

the run produces a durable, citable artifact regardless of outcome — a dated docs/evidence transcript under this repo's measured-here labelling, with conditions attached per docs/measuring-lane-performance.md rule 3. Falsified if the spike ends with only a verbal 'it didn't work' and no transcript

a docs/evidence/<date>-*-thor.txt transcript exists carrying: three arms x three content shapes with per-shape tok/s and acceptance, argv proven from docker inspect rather than .env, the same-day triton no-spec control, and an explicit statement of which arm was adopted and which rejected. A NEGATIVE result — the Triton path does not unlock speculation, or unlocks it at a net loss — satisfies this signal exactly as well as a positive one

a negative result is written up with the same care as a positive one. Verified by the transcript existing and being cited from docs/dspark-speculation.md regardless of outcome. Falsified if a failed unlock produces no evidence file — that is the specific failure mode c16 exists to prevent

no quality claim rides on this, and an observed divergence triggers INVESTIGATION before any verdict. Block speculation is lossless BY CONSTRUCTION (the target verifies every drafted token) — docs/dspark-speculation.md labels that STRUCTURAL, not measured, and explicitly notes it is 'not a claim that any particular implementation is bug-free: a broken verification path, a mangled config, or a silently-disabled speculative flag can all violate it in practice'. A Triton-vs-CUDA GDN decode swap is a further axis again, touching the non-speculative path too. So this spike measures speed and acceptance only; if an output difference IS observed on a speculative arm, the correct first move is to determine whether it is an implementation defect (config, verification path, parser) or a genuine algorithmic divergence — the structural claim is about the algorithm, and a defect falsifies the deployment, not the algorithm

an observed output divergence is reported IMMEDIATELY in the transcript and then investigated to a named cause — implementation defect or algorithmic divergence — with the losslessness claim SUSPENDED, not asserted, in the interim. Falsified by either failure mode: silently defending losslessness while a divergence sits unexplained, OR sitting on the observation until the investigation concludes. The investigation is bounded: if no cause is named, the claim is retracted rather than left suspended indefinitely

PRIMARY_MAX_NUM_SEQS must be pinned and held identical across all three arms, and its value stated in the transcript. The Thor's live .env carries PRIMARY_MAX_NUM_SEQS=2 with the comment 'MTP cap — 4 OOMs at n=3/high context', and env.example explicitly instructs 'Clear PRIMARY_MAX_NUM_SEQS too' when speculation is turned off — so the box currently runs an MTP-era OOM cap with no MTP. A re-render or an arm-specific edit could change it silently between arms, which would confound every throughput number. Choose one value deliberately, justify it, and prove it per arm from docker inspect

max_num_seqs is identical across all three arms and stated in the transcript. Verified from each arm's docker inspect argv. Falsified if any arm's --max-num-seqs differs, in which case that arm is re-run rather than reported with a caveat

every arm needs a discarded warmup generation before its measured run, because the Triton GDN path JIT-compiles. qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py carries @triton.jit kernels and vLLM's own message at line 167 warns a backend choice can cost JIT time ('Set --gdn-prefill-backend triton to skip JIT'). Switching gdn_decode_kernel to triton moves decode onto kernels that were never compiled on this box, so the first measured generation of the control arm — the arm every later delta is compared against — is the one most likely to carry compile cost and read artificially slow

measured throughput excludes JIT compile cost. Verified by discarding a warmup generation per arm and confirming a second run reproduces the first within the stated ~10-15% variance floor. Falsified if warmup and measured runs differ by more than that, which would mean compile cost is still leaking into the numbers

the DSpark arm executes third-party weights under --trust-remote-code, which the Thor's live cortex argv already carries. RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark is an outside publisher's repo, and a drafter is executable weights — spark-lobe.toml already says so ('an unpinned draft repo is a silent config change on the next pull') and pins the revision. That pin is the whole mitigation, so it must be carried verbatim into the Thor arm and proven from the container's rendered argv, never retyped from memory. Do not run the DSpark arm against a floating main

the DSpark arm runs the exact pinned revision 85ef153be924f17ce4bf62726954eeaa4a73e854. Verified from the container's rendered argv via docker inspect. Falsified by any floating or absent revision, in which case the arm is void and re-run

the spike needs a stated rollback to the known-good config, exercised at least once. d1 snapshotted ~/.lobes.pre-lightning-<ts> before its swap and that is the pattern to repeat, but the frame only says 'snapshot' without naming what restoring actually requires: this box's compose is HAND-EDITED (the primary lane's --speculative-config line was deleted, and the file predates the PRIMARY_SPECULATIVE_CONFIG slot), so restoring the .env alone does not restore the working lane. Rollback = restore the snapshot directory AND recreate the container, then re-prove 12.1 tok/s and the known_answer probe

rollback actually restores the working lane. Verified by exercising it at least once — restore the snapshot, recreate the container, and re-prove both the known_answer probe and ~12.1 tok/s on the cuda path. Falsified if the restored lane does not reproduce the 2026-08-20 numbers, which would mean the box drifted and the snapshot is not a rollback

the re-render required by c9 must PRESERVE this box's operator-typed peer keys, verified key by key against a pre-render copy of .env — but NOT for the HAND_FEASIBLE reason originally proposed, which a probe refuted. PROBED 2026-08-25: 'lobes init --fleet --shape spark-lobe --profile thor <scratch> --apply' into an empty directory renders HAND_FEASIBLE=false, not true — the thor card declares no hand role, so the shape's hosts list does not by itself stand up a local vllm-hand. What the same probe DID confirm is the real exposure: the fresh render emits max_model_len 262144, the DSpark speculative_config, and NO HAND_PEER_ORIGIN / HAND_PEER_API_KEY / MULTIMODAL_PEER_ORIGIN at all. Those three are operator-typed and per #92 never derived, so nothing regenerates them if a --force render drops them, and the Thor's hand and senses referrals would go dangling

no operator-typed peer key is lost by the re-render, and no local vllm-hand appears. Verified by diffing the post-render .env against a pre-render copy key by key, then confirming model=hand still answers with X-Lobes-Proxied-By pointing at the Spark and model=senses at the Orin. Falsified by any dropped *_PEER_ORIGIN / *_PEER_API_KEY, or by a vllm-hand container existing locally afterwards

tasks.summary: Build the rollback safety net and prove it works BEFORE touching anything
acceptance_criteria: ~/.lobes is copied to ~/.lobes.pre-speculation-<timestamp> following d1's naming, with .env captured separately for the key-by-key diff in t2
the rollback is EXERCISED once before any arm runs: restore the snapshot, recreate the cortex container, and re-prove BOTH the known_answer probe and ~12.1 tok/s on the cuda path
if the restored lane does not reproduce the 2026-08-20 numbers, the plan STOPS — the box has drifted and the snapshot is not a rollback
drop_caches (sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches) runs BEFORE the recreate, not after it fails; tegrastats confirms the free-block recovery
tasks.instruction: Do this FIRST and do not skip the exercise step — an unexercised snapshot is a hope, not a rollback. Follow d1's naming (~/.lobes.pre-speculation-<timestamp>). Remember this box's memory quirk: MemAvailable LIES here, so read tegrastats for the real free-block picture, and run drop_caches BEFORE the recreate rather than after the boot fails and the restart policy loops it.

tasks.summary: Re-render the deployment scaffold, preserving every operator-typed key
acceptance_criteria: a DRY-RUN 'lobes init --fleet --shape spark-lobe --profile thor' is diffed against the deployed compose and the live 'docker inspect' argv BEFORE any --apply, confirming the Thor does render spark-lobe (falsifies or confirms c8)
the render uses a plain --apply, NOT --apply --force; --force is used only if a specific key demands it and then reconciled by hand
post-render .env is diffed key by key against the pre-render copy; MULTIMODAL_PEER_ORIGIN/PROXY, HAND_PEER_ORIGIN/PROXY/API_KEY, WORKER_FEASIBLE and every *_FEASIBLE flag are present and unchanged
the rendered docker-compose.yml contains the ${PRIMARY_SPECULATIVE_CONFIG-...} slot (absent on the deployed 0.57.x-era file), verified by grep
no local vllm-hand container exists; model=hand still answers 200 with X-Lobes-Proxied-By pointing at the Spark, and model=senses likewise at the Orin
tasks.instruction: The riskiest step in the plan, because it regenerates a hand-edited deployment. Copy .env into the snapshot before rendering. Prefer a plain --apply: merge-only since 0.59.0 protects existing lines, whereas d1's --apply --force force-writes keys and nothing regenerates an operator-typed peer credential (#92). If --force proves necessary for a specific key, reconcile the rest by hand and re-verify both proxy paths.

IF any output difference is observed, the raw divergence is written into the transcript IMMEDIATELY, before diagnosis — sitting on the observation until the investigation concludes falsifies h13 just as much as defending losslessness does

risks.text: the DSpark drafter is a COLD PULL on this box — ~2.53 GiB of bf16 weights from RadixArk on Hugging Face, never fetched here. Neither the frame nor the challenge pass examined the Thor's HF cache state, disk headroom, or network path. A slow or failed pull stalls ARM C after the other two arms have already consumed the maintenance window, and a partial download can surface as a confusing load error rather than a clear network failure. Pre-fetch and verify the revision BEFORE the arm window opens

this plan has NO parallelism available — every arm mutates the same single physical box and the same cortex container, so 'devague plan waves' will emit narrow, effectively serial waves. That is honest, not a plan defect: do not fan this out to a workforce, and do not let wave width be read as an opportunity to run arms concurrently. Concurrent arms would also violate c14's same-day/same-harness/same-box-state condition

the Thor's cortex is DOWN for each container recreate across t2 through t5. Per the dual-cortex topology the mesh routes cortex to the Spark and the Orin proxies there, so blast radius is limited — but any local consumer on this box (the deployed lobes agent, culture-node containers) loses its local cortex for the duration. Announce the window; do not discover a dependent mid-arm

issue #204 — a shape override beats a card profile, so builtin/thor.toml cannot express a draft opinion that survives rendering spark-lobe. If t8 adopts a Thor-specific speculative config, the only supported homes are a new thor-cortex shape (orin-cortex.toml is the precedent) or forking spark-lobe. Neither is ergonomic; this plan does NOT close that gap

no lobes surface exposes draft acceptance — lobes/_metrics.py maps no spec-decode, draft or acceptance families for either engine, so every acceptance figure here comes from vLLM's docker_logs read by hand. Fine for a dated spike; it means an ADOPTED speculative lane degrades invisibly, since a drafter whose acceptance collapses on a workload shift looks identical to a slow box from every lobes surface

retiring the YaRN hf_overrides block at 262144 is deliberately OUT of this plan. The operator's quality rationale for the native ceiling argues for stock rope too, but every DSpark arm ever measured ran with that YaRN block in force, and folding it in would add a second uncontrolled variable to a three-arm comparison. It needs its own transcript at 262144 + stock rope
